stem: In the case of 'degloving' as described in the material, what clinical change has occurred?

options.text: The mucosa has been removed or stripped off the alveolar bone.
A tooth has been completely knocked out of its socket.
The enamel of the crown has been shattered into multiple pieces.
The tooth has been pushed sideways but remains in the bone.

explanation: Degloving refers to the traumatic separation of soft tissue (mucosa) from the underlying bony structure.
rationale: Think about an injury involving the covering of the bone.

optionExplanations.A: Degloving refers to the traumatic separation of soft tissue (mucosa) from the underlying bony structure.
optionExplanations.B: The complete removal of a tooth from its socket is called an avulsion, not degloving.
optionExplanations.C: This describes a crown fracture rather than the soft-tissue stripping associated with degloving.
optionExplanations.D: Moving a tooth in any direction within the socket is defined as luxation.

source.hint: Think about an injury involving the covering of the bone.
